notes: Bridge and lightstrips hold value best. A "Philips Hue UV Light Sanitizer Box" is not a smart bulb.

notes: Inovelli rarely hits liquidation; Zooz/Caseta are the realistic equivalents. Hue excluded - it has its own row.

label: ANC headphones (Sony XM series)
notes: Confirmed: "mx4" meant the Sony WH-1000XM line, and XM6 is acceptable. Range runs XM3-XM7. px7 was matching IPX7 waterproof ratings until anchored.

label: Pebble watch
notes: Pebble as a material word is everywhere - regex requires a product noun. Core Devices makes the 2025 relaunch.

label: Ubiquiti / UniFi
notes: AP or switch. U7 is the WiFi 7 line. Bare E7 removed - it matched a foot callus remover. Dream Machine needs a brand or a model suffix - Sony sells a "Dream Machine" clock radio.

label: AR / VR glasses
match_regex: (meta quest|oculus|quest [23]|\mxreal\M|\mnreal\M|rokid|viture|valve index|htc vive|vision pro|\mar glasses\M|\mvr headset\M)
notes: Headsets and display glasses only. Quest accessories are a large and noisy category.

label: Mini PC (Intel QuickSync)
notes: Best Jellyfin transcode path. OptiPlex / ThinkCentre / EliteDesk / ProDesk are brand names that already mean business desktop, so they match bare - the form-factor anchor was costing real buys: four HP ProDesk 600 G9 i5 lots cleared at $2.50 each and a bare EliteDesk i5 at $7, none of which said mini or SFF. The CPU pattern still needs a form-factor word beside it - a bare N95 match pulled in 15.6in laptops. Excludes gained the HP/Lenovo/Dell LAPTOP lines, since a bare brand match now runs closer to them, plus the keyboard/mouse/dock spares that carry a desktop model number. One backtest false positive: a COMeap ATX-to-SATA power cable "for Dell OptiPlex Series 3020 5040 7020 9020". The compatibility list is in the description, where the bare brand now matches, while the title truncates to "COMeap Motherboard ATX Mini 8 Pin to 2X..." before it reaches the word cable - and that lot carries no buried Title: line for the exclude to read either. Caught instead on motherboard/ATX/SATA/pin, which no mini PC listing uses.

label: Mini PC (AMD / other)
notes: Works for Jellyfin via VAAPI. "Mini PC Speakers" matched until speaker was excluded.

label: Rack PDU / UPS (Ubiquiti)
notes: Rack power for the homelab - Ubiquiti USP-PDU-Pro / SmartPower, or any rack-mount UPS. NOT a phone power bank; that was a misread and matched Dyson packs and hand warmers.

label: HDD / SSD
notes: TITLE ONLY. Watch for fake capacity - the 64TB Hard disik listings are counterfeit. Bare enclosure excluded; a drive-plus-enclosure bundle is the rare loss. Laptops and consoles added to the excludes: this row is TITLE ONLY and every cheap laptop and every Xbox prints its drive size in the title, so a 15.6in N5100 laptop and an Xbox Series X 1TB both matched as storage. mini_pc_quicksync already carried the laptop list for the same reason.

label: E-reader / e-ink (colour welcome)
notes: TITLE ONLY - descriptions say "compatible with e-readers" constantly. Colour e-ink explicitly wanted: Kaleido is the panel tech, so it catches Kobo Libra/Clara Colour and Boox Tab Ultra C by spec rather than model name. pocketbook and nook are anchored to product lines - bare "pocketbook" is a handbag and bare "nook" is a breakfast one. Power adapters and charm chains carry the brand name in the title and were the first two false positives.

label: HVAC tools & controls
notes: Vacuum pump now needs an AC/HVAC qualifier - it was matching food vacuum sealers.

label: WiFi 7 AP / router (any brand)
notes: AP or router only. X870/B850 motherboards advertise WiFi 7 and were flooding this.

label: Gravel / cyclocross bike
match_regex: (gravel (bike|bicycle|frame)|cyclocross|\mcx\M (bike|frame)|drop[- ]bar.{0,14}(bike|bicycle)|trek checkpoint|specialized (diverge|crux)|cannondale topstone|canyon (grail|grizl)|surly (straggler|midnight special|crosscheck)|salsa (fargo|cutthroat|warbird|journeyman)|giant revolt|marin nicasio|kona (rove|sutra)|norco search|bianchi impulso)
notes: Drop-bar gravel/CX. Model names are brand-anchored: bare "grail" matched the holy grail of skincare. PAC never states frame size, so sizing comes from photos.

label: Tablet - picture books + TV out
match_regex: (ipad air.{0,24}(m[1-4]\M|11[- ]inch|13[- ]inch|4th|5th)|ipad pro.{0,24}(m[1-4]\M|11|12\.9|13)|ipad.{0,12}(10th|11th|12th) gen|ipad mini.{0,12}(6th|7th)|ipad 1[13][- ]inch|ipad.{0,16}a1[467] chip|galaxy tab s(6|7|8|9|10)\M|lenovo tab (p11|p12))
notes: TITLE ONLY. Colour LCD for reading picture books to the kids, doubling as a travel media centre over USB-C. The whole row is a proxy for DisplayPort alt mode: iPad Air 4+/Pro USB-C/10th gen+/mini 6+ and Galaxy Tab S6+ have it. Deliberately NOT iPad 9th gen or older (Lightning) and NOT Galaxy Tab A (USB-C is charge-only) - the Tab A11+ that went for $160 could not drive a screen. Rootability was the earlier ask and is incompatible with this one: checkm8 stops at A11, every video-out model is A12 or newer. Cap set from observed sales - iPad Air M2 went for $190, iPad 10th gen for $225. Excludes learned from the backtest: "Cases" plural, a "Screen 13 inch Protector" split across words, and a French "tui avec clavier pour Galaxy Tab S6" folio.

label: Projector (native 4K / >1080p)
notes: NATIVE resolution above 1080p only, and the whole row is built to reject the word that dominates this category: every cheap LED unit says 4K. RCA RPJ167 "4K Support" cleared at $40 and $45, a "Mini Projector 4K" at $30.50, a "TMY 4K" at $7 - all of them 480p/720p panels that merely accept a 4K input and downscale, so "4k support" and friends are excluded outright and a bare 4k never matches. Real units are reached by brand beside a projector noun, because the brands alone are all something else in this corpus: Epson is ink and receipt printers, BenQ a monitor, Hisense TVs, JVC earbuds and a VCR. Laser TV is kept as an include (Hisense/Formovie UST are genuinely 4K) which is why the TV excludes name smart/Roku/QLED/OLED rather than a bare tv. TITLE ONLY - descriptions advertise 4K on everything. Expect long empty stretches: zero native-4K projectors have appeared in the corpus to date, so the $400 cap is an estimate, not an observed clearing price.

label: LG TV (OLED / QNED 50in+)
notes: TITLE ONLY - mount and remote listings say for LG OLED 55-85 inch constantly, so the description is not a safe haystack here. Three lookaheads that must all hold: LG, a premium panel word, and a 50in+ size. All three are load-bearing - the brand alone is a fridge shelf, a phone and a monitor in this corpus, and LG's own entry line is not wanted, so a 55in UA70 UHD is rejected on purpose alongside a 47in Cinema 3D 1080p and a 32in HD. QNED and NANO drop the leading word boundary so QNED80 and 65NANO75 match, but OLED keeps it: a bare oled matches Toledo, which is in this corpus as a Toledo Guardian Duplex Scale. Size is read from an inch or Class marker, or from the model number itself (OLED65C3PUA, 50QNED85A), which on some listings is the only place it appears at all. 48in and 42in OLED sit below the ask and are excluded. The cap rests on a single datapoint: LG 50in QNED85A took 38 bids to $262.50 and closed 2026-08-20, the only match in the whole corpus to date - so 450 is an estimate covering the larger OLED sizes, not a measured clearing price.

label: Air quality (PM2.5 + temp, local HA)
notes: PM2.5 with temperature, for Home Assistant. The category to hunt is smart air PURIFIERS, not monitors: dedicated air-quality sensors barely reach liquidation while purifiers flood it, and the good ones carry the sensor already. Ranked by how well they land in HA, local first - Dyson TP04/HP04/PH01 and newer report PM2.5, PM10, temp and humidity over local MQTT via ha-dyson, and turn up constantly because people bin them when the filter clogs. Xiaomi/Mi 3H/4/Pro are fully local through xiaomi_miio. VINDSTYRKA, Awair and Airthings are the purpose-built monitors, rarer. Model numbers do the work here because the brands alone are traps: bare dyson is overwhelmingly vacuums and hair tools, which is why the V-series, DC-series, Airwrap, Supersonic and Corrale are all excluded, and why TP01/TP02 are deliberately NOT matched - the sensor arrives with the 04 generation. Levoit must show its S suffix: a Core 300 and a Core 300S look identical in a title and only the S has WiFi or a sensor at all. Bare PMS5003 / SPS30 / SEN55 modules are included for the ESPHome route. NOTE this row matches PM2.5 mass in ug/m3; true per-channel particle counters are lab metrology (Fluke 985, AeroTrak, VPC300) and are matched but have no HA integration. Cap is an estimate, not an observed clearing price - no confirmed hit yet. Airmega matches standalone rather than anchored to coway: it is a Coway trademark and needs no brand beside it, whereas the proximity window missed a real one - a Coway Airmega ProX where the title said only COWAY and the model sat 200 characters into the description. LOCAL-FIRST. Fully local is the stated preference, and it splits this list in half. Local, no cloud account: Dyson TP04/HP04/PH01+ over local MQTT via ha-dyson; Xiaomi/Mi through xiaomi_miio; VINDSTYRKA over Zigbee; Awair Element, whose local API has to be switched on in the app first; and a bare PMS5003 / SPS30 / SEN55 on ESPHome, which is the only option that is local by construction rather than by vendor permission. Cloud-only, matched but second class: Levoit through VeSync, Coway Airmega through IoCare, Blueair. Those still alert because a two-dollar purifier is worth knowing about, but they are a cloud dependency and a rented integration, not a sensor you own. Airthings sits between the two - the HA integration is cloud, though BLE-capable models can be read locally via airthings_ble.

label: Robot vacuum + mop
notes: Mopping is mandatory, not a bonus - the house mops three times a day - so the row carries a second lookahead requiring it. That is what correctly rejects the Roomba 960 and the Shark AV2501AE, both self-emptying vacuums with no mop, which a naive robot-vacuum regex happily returns. Mop capability is read from the listing text OR from a model line that always mops: the three SEALED DEEBOT X1 PLUS units live right now never print the word mop anywhere, because OZMO is assumed - same reasoning as the Dyson TP04 rule in air_quality, where the feature arrives with a generation rather than a word. The noise in this category is robotic POOL cleaners, which outnumbered real hits on the first pass, plus window robots (ECOVACS WINBOT W2S), "Compatible for iRobot Roomba" filter packs, and cordless stick vacs carrying a robot brand - a bare dreame matched an R10 Pure stick vacuum and a GoVac405, so no brand matches alone. PREFER A MOP-WASHING DOCK: at three cleans a day a unit without one means rinsing pads by hand three times a day, which defeats the point. Cap is an estimate, not an observed clearing price: live at the time of writing were a DEEBOT N30 Omni (retail $453, seller states Functional: Yes) at $5 to enter and a roborock Saros 20 (MSRP $2299, FUNCTION TEST, defect: tiny scratch) at $127.50. WRITTEN AS X.*Y|Y.*X RATHER THAN TWO LOOKAHEADS ON PURPOSE. The obvious form, (?=.*X)(?=.*Y), is correct and 30x slower - it costs 17.9s against this corpus versus 601ms, because a lookahead drops Postgres off its DFA engine and onto the backtracking one, and this row is match_scope=full so the haystack is every description. lg_premium_tv gets away with three lookaheads only because it is title-only. Restating the conjunction in both orders is ugly and keeps the whole rebuild under five seconds.

label: Commuter bike (fast, XL)
notes: A bike for a 6ft4in rider to commute on WITHOUT it being slow, which makes this row mostly a set of exclusions. TITLE ONLY: Police Auctions is where every bike lives and it publishes no description at all, while HiBid descriptions advertise every brake rotor as fitting a road bike, hybrid bike and mountain bike at once - a full-scope version pulled in a Corki Cycles disc rotor on exactly that. DECODER, read off the photos: FS in a PAC title means FRONT SUSPENSION and DS means dual - verified against a Giant Rincon, which shows a coil fork and knobby 26in tyres. On a bike at this price that fork is undamped, heavy and eats your effort, so FS/DS is excluded outright and that single rule disqualifies six live lots (Giant Rincon, Giant Talon, both Diamondbacks, Hyper Viking, GT Timberline). What is wanted instead is a rigid fork and slick or semi-slick 700c tyres: the Trek 10-speed and the Kona Dew Plus both show exactly that. Lowstep and step-through are excluded because they are not a tall rider's frame; the department-store brands (Huffy, Supercycle, Hyper, Cyclemania, Mongoose, Roadmaster, Kent) are excluded because they are heavy at any price. E-bikes are included, since assist solves the speed problem outright, but not ones sold without their battery or charger - a Hitway BK6 (No Bat.) is a very heavy single-speed. SIZING: PAC states frame size on zero of 48 bike records, but it photographs every lot against a calibrated measuring wall - a vertical inch scale marked 6 to 42in and a horizontal foot scale reading 3ft either side of a plumbed centre line. So frame size comes from the photos, which is what the Refresh button is for: the browse scrape banks one thumbnail, the lot page carries eight full-size shots and roughly one of them is square side-on. Good enough to sort XL from M by standover and saddle height; NOT good enough to call 21in against 22in, and a seatpost already near maximum extension is the tell for a frame that is too small. Cap is an estimate: live at the time of writing were a Trek 1x10 hydraulic-disc flat-bar at $157 and a Kona Dew Plus at $204.50.
